And in that first year of his reign, he sent fifty thousand of the people—
though not all of them,
because the seventy [years] were not yet completed—
by the hands of Zerubbabel and Joshua the son of Jozadak.
And he commanded that they build the Temple in Jerusalem according to the prophecy of Isaiah.
Now the building was hindered by the surrounding nations for forty-six years,
as John the Evangelist wrote,
until the sixth year of Darius the son of Hystaspes (Ushtasap).
After Cyrus the Persian, Cambyses his son [reigned] eight years.
The Hebrews say that this man was called Nebuchadnezzar.
And in his time Judith became known, she who killed Holofernes the Magogite, that is, the Turk.
And in his sixth year they completely destroyed Tyre.
After Cambyses, two Magian brothers [reigned] seven months,
and they are counted with the years of Cambyses.
After the two Magian brothers, Darius the son of Hystaspes [reigned] thirty-six years.
In his second year,
the seventy years of the captivity were completed,
according to Clement, Eusebius, and Andronicus, and the testimony of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah.
And in his sixth year the House was finished in the month of Iyyar;
its height was sixty cubits,
and its breadth twenty.
The total years from the first building of Solomon until this year of the completion of the second building was five hundred and eight years.
In this [year/time] {OCR?} Pythagoras the philosopher died,
having lived ninety-five [years?].
And Democritus and Diogenes the philosophers,
and Anaxagoras the natural philosopher,
and Pindar and Simonides the lyric poets {OCR?},
and Hippocrates the physician,
and Protagoras and Isocrates the Sophists,
and Aristophanes and Eupolis {OCR?} the founders of comedy were famous.
And more than all of them, the great Hippocrates, the teacher of physicians, was renowned throughout the world even to this day.
Now he lived in the city of Homs,
and from time to time {OCR?} he would go to Damascus,
and he would stay in its gardens, in which even to this day {OCR?} there is known a place called the Porch of Hippocrates.
And he was a divine man,
who healed the sick for free.
